eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are mostly mechanical and discriminating (check_run.py covers 10 of 15). The judgment assertions passed on genuine substance. The run also surfaced three real-looking code issues as reviewer notes instead of silently patching, which is the right call for a submit skill but is not rewarded by any assertion.

notes: Strong run: 15/15 with no borderline fails. The assertions are well targeted at the hard parts (lede length, numbers from BENCHMARKS.md, lint on both body and commits) and the mechanical ones are backed by check_run.py. Two gaps worth closing: the skim test should say whether a table row counts as a skimmed first sentence, since the latency cost here lives in the table and in mid-paragraph sentences; and nothing checks that the breaking limiter rename is called out in the PR body, which is the single most important reviewer fact in this fixture and a weaker run could skip it unpunished. The test-passed assertion rests on the transcript summary alone.
